integrity: No quotes; paraphrased. No likeness generation for real athletes.

stories.name: Hunter
stories.hs: a suburban high school in South Carolina

timeline.fact: quarterback at a suburban high school, ~150 lb; recruited by a D1 program that offered aid (scholarship) while a Power 4 program offered only preferred walk-on status
Changed position to receiver, gained ~30 lb, roughly raised lift from ~180 to 280+ lb
Awarded scholarship before the 2016 season
Caught game-winning TD with 1 second left against the top-ranked team in national title game

turning: Chose a preferred walk-on spot at his dream school over a scholarship
replicate: Ask every preferred walk-on offer what the path to scholarship looks like
Weigh guaranteed money vs. fit honestly as a family

stories.name: Sara
stories.hs: Derrick Rock, British Columbia (Canada); club: Washington Sidewinders
stories.path: under-recruited club player found at tournaments

timeline.fact: Said she was not highly recruited; only a couple of schools showed serious interest
the D1 head coach first saw her at club tournaments outside the usual recruiting map
an assistant coach persistently emailed; she visited and committed after feeling at home

turning: Club tournament exposure in a non-hotbed region
Agreed to visit a school she had never heard of
replicate: Pick club events where target coaches actually attend
Say yes to visits outside your geography

stories.name: Karsta

timeline.fact: Two-sport athlete (tennis and volleyball) until sophomore year, so specialized late
Only a handful of East Coast programs offered scholarships; she did not feel comfortable that far from home
Committed to walk on at a D1 program with no scholarship money available
Emerged as one of one of the best players on the roster as a junior

replicate: Late-specializing athletes still have windows
Treat walk-on as a real option at the right fit

stories.name: Olivia

timeline.fact: Played club/travel baseball on the national club circuit and made the US Women's National Baseball Team
Had several college offers but chose a D1 program with no guarantee; went through walk-on tryouts
Named to the varsity roster, the first woman on a D1 baseball roster

replicate: Ask admissions-first schools about fall walk-on tryouts

stories.name: Derrick
stories.hs: a new suburban high school, Parker, CO (first graduating class)
stories.college: a D2 school, then a D1 transfer

timeline.fact: 6-0 senior with no D1 offers; father sent highlight video to ~25 JUCO and D2 schools
Only full offer was Gillette (WY) JC; a D2 school coach Jeff Culver offered a ~$3,000 housing stipend/preferred walk-on
Culver: Derrick was first recruit he brought for a campus visit; redshirt plan scrapped
D2 All-American; transferred to a D1 school, sat 2015-16, led CU in scoring 2016-17

turning: Following a coach who believed in him
replicate: Email video broadly to JUCO/D2, not just D1
Track coaches who move jobs

stories.name: Samantha
stories.hs: a suburban high school in Ohio
stories.sourcing: thin on recruiting details (outcome well sourced)

timeline.fact: Recruited to a D2 program by then the head coach; credits his high school coach
the D2 national player of the year; 35-3, Elite Eight
a national academic and athletic award finalist; PA health-sciences major

turning: Stayed close to home at D2
replicate: Use high school coach as the first contact to nearby D2s
Pair athletics with a professional major

stories.name: Ali
stories.sourcing: moderate (high school name from general knowledge, verify)

timeline.fact: Undersized (~235 lb), played football and basketball; no D1 offers
a D3 program pitched economics/Wall Street path; later grew and football became priority
Drafted round 2 by an NFL team, highest-drafted D3 player ever

replicate: Treat D3 as a development path, not a consolation

stories.name: Annie
stories.hs: a private high school in Ohio

timeline.fact: Started running at 17; soccer conflicted with XC so she ran track only; original plan was soccer scholarship
Came to a D3 program with little running experience; her coach saw potential
an NCAA D3 national champion

turning: Switched sports late on coach advice
replicate: Multi-sport kids: test a second sport junior year
Target D3 coaches who develop raw athletes

stories.name: Tori
stories.hs: a suburban high school in Florida

timeline.fact: Became a goalie when a friend needed one; soccer background
Set goal of playing in college during first season
Committed to a D3 program for city location and team diversity
Graduated biology; a national team

replicate: Write the goal down early
Score schools on culture, not just level

stories.name: Cedric
stories.hs: Central high school, a public high school in California
stories.college: a D3 school (D3), later D1 transfers
stories.sourcing: thin (single blog source; verify college names)

timeline.fact: Switched from football to basketball focus; grew to 6-4 by senior year; not highly recruited
Averaged 19.5 pts / 12 reb at D3
First-round NBA draft prospect after D1 transfer

replicate: D3 film can open D1 doors via portal

stories.name: Cristelle
stories.path: quit in high school, recruited into new program

timeline.date: junior and senior year of high school
timeline.fact: Stepped away from wrestling due to pressure and mental health
Joined an NAIA program first women's wrestling recruiting class under a new head coach
the first national champion in program history (123)
U20 World Champion 55kg

replicate: Look at brand-new programs
A gap year from the sport is not the end

stories.name: Jimmy
stories.hs: a large suburban high school in Texas
stories.college: a JUCO program, then a D1 school

timeline.fact: Averaged ~19 pts as senior but not heavily recruited
an all-American mention at the JUCO level at a JUCO program (18.1 ppg)
Signed a letter of intent with a D1 school as the first signee of a new head coach

replicate: JUCO as a one-year showcase
Watch for programs with sudden roster holes

stories.name: Composite: "Maya" (swimmer)
stories.label: Composite story built from 3 sourced recruiting paths
basis: Swimmer recruiting relies on club coach advocacy and posted times (https://www.wabash.edu/news/story/2362)
Walk-on to scholarship pattern (Alika Crawford, UNT track: https://www.athletes.org/news/my-story-alika-crawford)
Parent-sent video to many lower-division programs (Derrick: https://www.nba.com/spurs/derrick-white-dare-be-great)
replicate: Keep a times sheet updated and send to D2/D3 coaches
Ask club coach to call
